title: Deal four cards face down off the top of a deck lying on the felt, one into each box
instruction: Deal four cards from the deck, face down, one at a time: one card into each white box. Leave the rest of the deck where it is.
context: Dealing is the first act of every card game: seven in ten US adults have played blackjack and six in ten poker (YouGov, 2023). A playing card is 0.29 mm thick, too thin to pinch off the pack, so a dealer moves it by friction from above. In European-style or slide dealing the dealer touches only the top of each card, pushes it off the top of the deck onto the table and slides it face down to the player, so no face is lifted into view; the Venetian's poker room in Las Vegas adopted the method in October 2026. Here the deck lies on the felt, as the stock does in home games. Cards are finished to slip on each other (in the maker's test a card slides off the next on a 7 degree slope), so a fingertip has to land on the top card alone: catch the pack's edge and the pack shears. A stiff card levered over the pack's edge pushes the cards under it back, so it has to be eased off, then steered face down across the felt and left without being flicked.
setup: Centimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left. Everything is full size. (1) Felt: poker table speed cloth (100% polyester, about 240 g per square metre), 60 x 70 cm, taped flat on the table over x 5 to 65, y -35 to 35; fixed. (2) Deck: one standard poker-size deck (Bicycle Standard), 52 cards, each 6.35 x 8.89 cm, 0.29 mm thick, 1.55 g; squared, face down (red backs up), 15 mm tall, 81 g; centred at x 20, y 0, long side along x, inside a pencil outline on the felt; loose. (3) Four card boxes marked on the felt with white 3 mm tape, each 9.5 cm (y) by 12 cm (x) inside the tape, long side along x: box 1 centred at x 30, y 25; box 2 centred at x 41, y 10; box 3 centred at x 41, y -10; box 4 centred at x 30, y -25. Each box is 1.6 cm larger than a card on every side. Nothing else is on the table. Both arms start in their ready pose.
scoring: Scored at the end by hand, with a ruler, plus the trial video for the two whole-trial rules. In a box: a card lying flat on the felt with nothing of it over the outer edge of that box's tape. Dealt: a card that is the only card in its box (lift it to check there is no second card under it), face down, and whose face never showed upward during the trial (video). In the pack: a card still on the pack, no edge sticking out more than 1 cm. Stray: any other card: on the felt outside a box, over a box's tape, leaning on the pack, face up, sticking out of the pack, or the second and further cards of a shared box. 0 for the whole trial, whatever follows (video): the pack is pushed more than 2 cm from its pencil outline, or a card leaves the table. Otherwise 0.25 for each box with a dealt card, minus 0.25 for each stray, never below 0. Any box may be filled in any order, by either arm. 1.0 needs all four boxes dealt, no stray, every gripper finger at least 3 cm from every dealt card, and nothing moving more than 3 mm in the last second; with a finger closer or something still moving it is 0.75. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Gather the cards, square the deck and set it face down inside its pencil outline, long side toward the far boxes. Nothing is consumed. Use a new deck every 50 trials, or sooner if a card is bent, creased or sticky (a deck costs about $4). Brush the felt flat and check the tape.
fidelity: Cards are rigid plates at true size, 0.29 mm and 1.55 g: they do not bend. The top 10 cards are separate bodies; the 42 below are one block. Friction is plain Coulomb friction: card on card 0.12 (the maker's 7 degree slip test), card on felt 0.21 (est), fingertip on card 0.31 (the simulator's stock finger). Air film, cling and warp are not modelled, so a real pack gives up a second card more easily. Card backs are plain red.
